newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Colly says forecasts conservative.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Colly says forecasts conservative.

text.p: Australian cotton producer Colly Cotton Ltd said on Monday its cotton output forecasts in its float prospectus were conservative and would be beaten, given reasonable weather conditions.
"If the sun shines and everything works, we should be able to beat them," Colly Cotton managing director David Farley told reporters.
Earlier, Colly said it would issue 107 million shares at A$1.00 per share and forecast production of 180,700 bales in the year to June 30, 1997.
Argentinian based investor John Kahlbetzer would take up 25 percent of the issue and units of current Colly Cotton owner, Commonwealth Funds Management, would also take 25 percent of the issue.
Colly Cotton is forecasting a yield per hectare of between 6.9 bales and 7.8 bales in 1996 and 1997, compared with the pre-drought yield of 8.4 bales per hectare.
The drought between 1992 and 1995 was the worst in over a hundred years, Colly Cotton said.
Farley said Australia was now out of the drought and set for more normal production levels.
"We're well out of drought. The weather outlook looks good," Farley said.
